action: General advice: buy Hong Kong Disneyland tickets only through official resort channels or authorised travel agents, not unofficial resellers, as stolen codes may circulate.
date_note: Resort announced the incident on Friday 13 Nov; staff found unusual activity on the evening of 12 Nov.
exec: A major tourist venue paused online sales after ticket codes were reportedly stolen, showing ticketing systems are direct targets.
plain: Hong Kong Disneyland found a cyber incident in its online ticketing system and stopped selling tickets and hotel rooms online. About 17,000 ticket QR codes were reported stolen. Online ticket sales were reported back by 18 November.

sources.name: 10jqka (relaying Time Weekly / 时代财经), 18 Nov 2026

summary: Hong Kong Disneyland said it detected a cybersecurity incident, suspended online ticket and hotel sales, reported it to police and tightened gate checks. The Standard reports about 17,000 e-ticket QR codes were stolen; the resort did not itself verify that number. No arrests were reported. Time Weekly, relayed by 10jqka, says park ticket sales had resumed on the official site by 18 November, while online hotel booking stayed suspended for system maintenance.
title: Hong Kong Disneyland suspends online sales after about 17,000 ticket QR codes reported stolen

validation.note: The Standard and eSecurity Planet (citing SCMP); resort statement relayed; code count not independently verified by the resort. Sales resumption on 18 Nov from Time Weekly (relayed by 10jqka) only.

review.note: Compared 12-13 Nov dates, about 17,000 QR codes unverified by resort, police classification, no arrests, PCPD, suspension against The Standard and eSecurity Planet
